Dygraph = require(await FileAttachment("lib/dygraph/dygraph.min.js").url())

function showAnnotationModal(ann) {
  const existing = document.getElementById("dygraph-annotation-modal");
  if (existing) existing.remove();

  const backdrop = document.createElement("div");
  backdrop.id = "dygraph-annotation-backdrop";
  backdrop.style.position = "fixed";
  backdrop.style.top = "0";
  backdrop.style.left = "0";
  backdrop.style.width = "100vw";
  backdrop.style.height = "100vh";
  backdrop.style.backgroundColor = "rgba(0,0,0,0.4)";
  backdrop.style.zIndex = "9999";

  const modal = document.createElement("div");
  modal.id = "dygraph-annotation-modal";
  modal.style.position = "fixed";
  modal.style.top = "50%";
  modal.style.left = "50%";
  modal.style.transform = "translate(-50%, -50%)";
  modal.style.backgroundColor = "#ffffff";
  modal.style.padding = "20px";
  modal.style.borderRadius = "8px";
  modal.style.boxShadow = "0 4px 20px rgba(0,0,0,0.3)";
  modal.style.zIndex = "10000";
  modal.style.maxWidth = "450px";
  modal.style.width = "90%";
  modal.style.fontFamily = "Arial, sans-serif";

  modal.innerHTML = `
    <div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; border-bottom: 1px solid #eee; padding-bottom: 8px; margin-bottom: 12px;">
      <strong style="font-size: 16px; color: #333;">${ann.series || 'Annotation'}</strong>
      <button id="close-ann-modal" style="background: none; border: none; font-size: 22px; cursor: pointer; color: #888;">&times;</button>
    </div>
    <div style="font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.5; color: #444;">
      ${ann.text}
    </div>
  `;

  const closeModal = () => {
    modal.remove();
    backdrop.remove();
  };

  backdrop.addEventListener("click", closeModal);
  document.body.appendChild(backdrop);
  document.body.appendChild(modal);

  document.getElementById("close-ann-modal").addEventListener("click", closeModal);
}

html`${allGroups.map((group, groupIdx) => {
// the following 5 lines solve the problem of filtering and mapping when there is only one time series in a group
  const titles = Array.isArray(group.titles) ? group.titles : [group.titles];
  const visibility = Array.isArray(group.visibility) ? group.visibility : [group.visibility];
  const colors = Array.isArray(group.colors) ? group.colors : [group.colors];
  const timestamps = Array.isArray(group.timestamps) ? group.timestamps : [group.timestamps];
  const labels = [].concat(group.labels);
  
  const checkboxInputs = Inputs.checkbox(
    titles, 
    { 
      value: titles.filter((_, i) => visibility[i])
    }
  );
  
  const indinfo = Inputs.checkbox(
    titles, 
    { 
      value: titles.filter((_, i) => visibility[i])
    }
  );
  
  const legdivht = 50 + (titles.length*30);
  
  
  // Generate dynamic CSS rules to style each checkbox label & input by color
  const dynamicStyles = html`<style>
    ${colors.map((color, idx) => `
      /* Scope styles specifically to this group index */
      .group-cb-${groupIdx} label:nth-child(${idx + 1}) {
        color: ${color} !important;
        font-weight: 400;
        display: block;
      }
      .group-cb-${groupIdx} label:nth-child(${idx + 1}) input[type="checkbox"] {
        accent-color: ${color} !important;
        color: white;
      }
    `).join("")}
    #legdiv_${groupIdx} {height : ${legdivht} px;}
  </style>`;

  const chartContainer = document.createElement("div");
  chartContainer.style.width = "100%";
  chartContainer.style.height = "300px";
  chartContainer.style.position = "relative";
  chartContainer.style.marginTop = "10px";
  chartContainer.style.marginBottom = "40px";

  const chartData = timestamps.map((t, rowIdx) => {
    const row = [new Date(t)];
    for (let colIdx = 0; colIdx < labels.length; colIdx++) {
      row.push(group.values[rowIdx][colIdx]);
    }
    return row;
  });
  
  let checkedCount = checkboxInputs.value.length;
  
  checkboxInputs.addEventListener("input", () => {
    const selectedTitles = checkboxInputs.value;
    const currentVisibility = titles.map(title => selectedTitles.includes(title));
    checkedCount = selectedTitles.length;
    
    if (chartContainer._dygraphInstance) {
      chartContainer._dygraphInstance.updateOptions({ visibility: currentVisibility });
    }
  });

  requestAnimationFrame(() => {
    const initialVisibility = titles.map(title => checkboxInputs.value.includes(title));

    // Define underlay shading for Habitat Compression (Group 0)
    let underlayFn = null;
    if (groupIdx === 0 && group.stats) {
      underlayFn = function(canvas, area, g) {
// ONLY draw shading if EXACTLY ONE checkbox is selected
        if (checkedCount !== 1) return;

        const selectedTitles = checkboxInputs.value;
        const visibleIdx = titles.findIndex(t => selectedTitles.includes(t));
        
        const stats = (visibleIdx !== -1 && group.stats[visibleIdx]) ? group.stats[visibleIdx] : group.stats[2]; 
        if (!stats) return;

        const y0 = g.toDomYCoord(stats[3]);                 // Max
        const y1 = g.toDomYCoord(stats[0] + stats[1]);       // +1 SD
        const y2 = g.toDomYCoord(stats[0]);                 // Mean
        
        // Ensure y3 hits Y = 0 or the bottom of the canvas plot area (area.y + area.h)
        const y0Dom = g.toDomYCoord(0);
        const y3 = (y0Dom !== null && !isNaN(y0Dom)) ? Math.min(y0Dom, area.y + area.h) : area.y + area.h; 

        // Calculate positive heights
        const y0height = Math.max(0, y1 - y0);
        const y1height = Math.max(0, y2 - y1);
        const y2height = Math.max(0, y3 - y2); // Fills from Mean down to Y=0 / bottom

        // Draw low (green), medium (yellow), and high (red) compression bands
        canvas.fillStyle = "rgba(0, 255, 0, 0.12)";
        canvas.fillRect(area.x, y0, area.w, y0height);

        canvas.fillStyle = "rgba(255, 255, 0, 0.12)";
        canvas.fillRect(area.x, y1, area.w, y1height);

        canvas.fillStyle = "rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.12)";
        canvas.fillRect(area.x, y2, area.w, y2height);

        // Text Labels
        canvas.font = "14px Arial";
        canvas.fillStyle = "rgba(100, 100, 100, 0.85)";
        canvas.fillText("low", area.x + area.w - 60, y0 + (y0height / 2) + 5);
        canvas.fillText("medium", area.x + area.w - 60, y1 + (y1height / 2) + 5);
        canvas.fillText("high", area.x + area.w - 60, y2 + (y2height / 2) + 5);      };
    }
    const dyInstance = new Dygraph(chartContainer, chartData, {
      labels: ["Time", ...labels],
      colors: colors,
      visibility: initialVisibility,
      underlayCallback: underlayFn, // Applies underlay shading if defined
      ylabel: group.ylabel || "",
      y2label: group.y2label || "",
      series: group.series || {},  // Assigns specified series to 'y2' axis
      legend: "always",
      hideOverlayOnMouseOut: false,
      showRangeSelector: true,
      labelsSeparateLines: true,
      labelsDiv: "legdiv_"+group.index,
      strokeWidth: group.strokewidth,
      pointSize: group.pointsize,
      highlightCircleSize: group.highlightcirclesize,
      dateWindow: group.datewindow,
      xRangePad: group.xrangepad,
      yRangePad: group.yrangepad,
      rightGap: group.rightgap
    });

// Attach annotations if present for this group
  if (group.annotations && group.annotations.length > 0) {
    dyInstance.ready(() => {
      const validSeries = labels;
      
      const readyAnnotations = group.annotations.map((ann, idx) => {
        const matchedSeries = validSeries.includes(ann.series) ? ann.series : validSeries[0];
        
        return {
          x: ann.x,
          series: matchedSeries,
          shortText: ann.shortText || "A",
          text: ann.text,
          icon: ann.icon,
          width: ann.width || 20,
          height: ann.height || 20,
          cssClass: "dygraph-annotation",
          annotationId: idx // Unique reference ID
        };
      });

      dyInstance.setAnnotations(readyAnnotations);
      
      // Store reference on instance
      dyInstance._annotationList = readyAnnotations;
    });

    // Delegated click handler on the chart DOM container
    chartContainer.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
      const annEl = e.target.closest(".dygraph-annotation");
      if (annEl && dyInstance._annotationList) {
        e.stopPropagation();
        e.preventDefault();

        // Find matching annotation object from dyInstance._annotationList
        const annTitle = annEl.getAttribute("title");
        const matchedAnn = dyInstance._annotationList.find(a => a.text === annTitle) || dyInstance._annotationList[0];
        
        if (matchedAnn) {
          showAnnotationModal(matchedAnn);
        }
      }
    });
  }

    chartContainer._dygraphInstance = dyInstance;
    
    setTimeout(() => {
      chartContainer._dygraphInstance.resize();
    }, 50);
  });

  return html`
    ${dynamicStyles}
    <div id="grp${groupIdx}" class="custom-container" style="padding: 15px; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e9ecef; border-radius: 6px; margin-bottom: 25px;">
      <div class="custom-sidebar group-cb-${groupIdx}">
      <span class="custom-sidebar-title">Choose indicator:</span>
      ${checkboxInputs}
      </div>
      <div class="custom-main">
      <div><h3>${group.title}</h3></div>
      <div id="legdiv_${group.index}"></div>
      ${chartContainer}
      </div>
    </div>
  `;
})}`

Habitat Compression

Habitat Compression Index

The habitat compression index uses 2 m temperature from the historic and NRT data assimilative ROMS physical model of the California Current system (http://oceanmodeling.ucsc.edu/index.html). Grid points between 30-48 degrees N and from the shore out to 150 km offshore are used in the analysis. In eastern boundary upwelling ecosystems the spatial footprint of cool upwelled water is regularly demarcated by the differential boundary of warmer oceanic water offshore from cooler coastal water, with upwelling conditions varying with latitude. Therefore, the goal of the habitat compression index (HCI) is to track the area of cool surface waters as an index of potential ‘upwelling habitat’ for assessing the spatio-temporal aspects of upwelling. Upwelling patterns of cold nutrient-rich water are clearly assessed by models and satellite observations and classified spatially by monitoring SST values less than and equal to a monthly resolved temperature threshold. The HCI tracks the amount of area, determined by the number of grid cells in the model with 2 m surface temperature values less than the monthly temperature threshold, therefore the time series reflects the area of cool water adjacent to the coastline and provides a measure for how compressed cool surface temperatures may be in a particular month. In this study (Schroeder et al. 2022), we extracted modeled 2 m temperature fields over the domain of 35.5-40 degree N for each month and tracked the amount of area with temperature values less than and equal to a monthly temperature threshold, resulting in monthly time series starting January 1980. Monthly temperature thresholds for a given month is the spatial average of 2 m temperature grid cells between 35.5-40N from shore out to 75 km for the time period 1980-2010. Cool expansion periods (low compression) are defined as months with HCI values exceeding + 1 standard deviation (SD) of the full time series, limited cool habitat (high compression) where area of cool water is less than the mean (MN) of the full time series, and periods of medium compression when the area of cool water falls between the +1 SD and the MN.

Institution: NOAA SWFSC/FED

Time Range: 1980-01-01 - 2026-08-01

North Pacific High Jan - Feb Mean

Variations in large-scale atmospheric forcing influence upwelling dynamics and ecosystem productivity in the California Current System.The area of the North Pacific High (NPH) is characterized by areal extent of the 1020 Pa isobar. Winter values (January - February mean) of the NPH area can be used as an ecosystem pre-conditioning index (Schroeder et al., doi:10.1002/grl.50100).The area of the NPH are calculated from monthly mean sea level pressure (SLP) fields created by the U.S. Navy Fleet Numerical Meterology and Oceanography Center (FNMOC). Monthly SLP data available at https://coastwatch.pfeg.noaa.gov/erddap/griddap/erdlasFnWPr.html. The area is the areal extent of the 1020 hPa contour for a given month. The January - February mean is the average of the January and February areas for a given year. The NRT ROMS temperature data downloaded from the UCSC website (http://oceanmodeling.ucsc.edu/index.html) has grid points with 2 m temperature data reported as Not-A-Number, these values are 2 m temperatu. Tdata at these grid points are obtained by extrapolating the data to 2 m depth using the interp1d routine from the Python library scipy.interpolate sub-package.

Upwelling Index - CUTI 45N monthly

CUTI is a new upwelling index that leverages state-of-the-art ocean models as well as satellite and in situ data to improve upon historically available upwelling indices for the U.S. west coast. CUTI provides estimates of vertical transport near the coast (i.e., upwelling/downwelling). It was developed as a more accurate alternative to the previously available Bakun Index. See Jacox, M. G., C. A. Edwards, E. L. Hazen, and S. J. Bograd (2018) Coastal upwelling revisited: Ekman, Bakun, and improved upwelling indices for the U.S. west coast. Journal of Geophysical Research, doi:10.1029/2018JC014187. NA

Whale Abundance

Humpback whale relative abundance, central CA

Data provided by J. Santora (NOAA/UCSC; jsantora@ucsc.edu). The humpback whale relative abundance anomaly is based on visual surveys collected in the core area of the RREAS survey. For more information, consult Figure 2c: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-14215-w#data-availability. Observational data were collected during the annual NOAA-NMFS Rockfish Recruitment and Ecosystem Assessment Survey. Approximately 120 mid-water trawls are collected per survey and depending on weather, typically each sampling station or area isoccupied 2-3 times per survey (standardized since 1983) both on and off the continental shelf. Visual surveys for whales are collected continuously during daylight hours; sampling units are presented as sighting number of whales per 3 km interval; the anomaly is an index of abundance standardized by encounter rate (# of whales per 100 km of survey effort). Sightings data on marine mammals were collected by a trained observer and entered in real time using a sightings database. NA

Institution: Farallon Institute, RREAS surveys

Time Range: 1996-01-01 - 2019-01-01

Prey Abundance - Central CA

Krill

Dr. John Field (NOAA; john.field@noaa.gov) and Tanya Rogers (NOAA; tanya.rogers@noaa.gov) from the SWFSC Rockfish Recruitment and Ecosystem Assessment Survey (RREAS; https://storymaps.arcgis.com/collections/af0fa37db2bf4f1cadb024ec0ffbdfb5). Samples represent catch (individuals) per standard 15 minute trawl (CPUE) from the historical core area (36.5-38.2N) of the RREAS during late spring (May to mid-June). Data are log(CPUE+1) transformed, with geometric means calculated on non-zero data. Note: Sampling effort was greatly reduced in time and space during 2020 due to COVID restrictions, and associated data reflected substantial bias for many taxa. Catches were standardized by using a Bayesian delta-GLM to estimate year effects while accounting for spatial and temporal covariates, and to estimate approximate 95% confidence limits; see Santora et al. 2021 (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-26484-5) for model approaches used to develop alternative indices in 2020.

Crab Fisheries Activity Maps

About these maps

The information presented in these maps is based on modeled predictions of fishing activity using vessel telemetry data (vessel monitoring system, VMS) that has been linked to landings data associated with each trip (Feist et al. 2021). The maps were generated in order to assess trends in fishing activity and how they might relate to large whale entanglements off the west coast of the United States from 2009 through mid-2016. Vessel speed and depth filters were used to identify where fishing activity was occurring, which is considered an approximation of where fishing may or may not be occurring. Further, not all vessels that fish for Dungeness crab are equipped with VMS transponders, with the proportion monitored being ~10%, ~50% and ~30% for Washington, Oregon and California, respectively. Fishing activity maps based on vessel telemetry should be used with caution, given the limitations and biases associated with the modeling methodology. Finally, the fishing activity mapping on these pages are based on the best available science at the time of their posting, but will be updated in the future as methods and source data, e.g., logbooks available in the states of Oregon and Washington, to better characterize fishing activity evolve and become available

Crab Fisheies Research 

    <p>On the U.S. West Coast, reports of whales entangled in fishing gear increased dramatically in 2014. In this study, a time-series of fishing activity maps were developed from 2009-2016 for the four fixed-gear fisheries most commonly implicated in entanglements. Maps were generated using vessel monitoring system (VMS) data linked to port-level landings databases, which were related to entangled whale reports over the same time period and with modelled distributions of humpback whales (<i>Megaptera novaeangliae</i>). Over the full study period, neither marked increases in fishing activity nor changes in fisheries footprints within regions with high whale densities were detected. In contrast, a delayed fishery opening in California due to a harmful algal bloom in spring of 2016 led to ~5–7 times average levels of Dungeness crab (<i>Metacarcinus magister</i>) fishing activity, which was consistent with a high rate of entanglement in that year. These results are consistent with current hypotheses that habitat compression caused by a marine heat wave increased the overlap of whales with fishing activity, despite minimal changes in the fisheries themselves. This study adds to literature on bycatch of protected species in otherwise sustainable fisheries, highlighting the value of using VMS data for reducing human-wildlife conflict in the ocean.<p>Geospatial data layers of Dungeness crab fishing activity off the U.S. West Coast at a 5km grid resolution using landings informed VMS data for posting to the CCIEA website. Data are binned in 4-month or annual intervals from the 2010-11 Dungeness crab season through June of 2016. Grid cells with fewer than 3 boats represented for any given time interval receive a value of 0. The data are considered non-confidential. Suggested value ranges for 4-month interval VMS ping count classes: &lt;21; 21-35; 36-70; 71-140; 141-280; 281-560; &gt;560. Suggested value ranges for annual interval VMS ping count classes: &lt;50; 50-100; 101-200; 201-400; 401-800; 801-1600; &gt;1600. See: Feist, BE, JF Samhouri, KA Forney &amp; LE Saez (2021) Footprints of fixed gear fisheries in relation to rising whale entanglements on the U.S. West Coast. Fisheries Management &amp; Ecology  28(3): 283-294.  DOI:  10.1111/fme.12478</p>
